In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the macrocyclic compounds show a similar electronic structure to the linear ones and a different one to the tetrameric ones, and that the macrocyclicity is not a major factor in the optical and electrochemical behavior.
the phenylene-bridges in the macrocycles are not detrimental to the properties of the azaacenes, but rather they are able to stabilize the molecules and thus enable their synthesis in good yields.
the electronic and optical properties of the phenylene-bridges are not significantly different from those of the corresponding N-heteroarenes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the macrocyclic compounds are less planar than the linear analogues, but they show a higher degree of aromaticity, as evidenced by the higher HOMO/LUMO energy gap and the larger aromatic resonance energy.
the macrocycles are not only interesting as a new class of macrocyclic N-heteroarenes but also as potential candidates for organic electronic devices.

the phenylene bridge has a profound influence on the optical properties and the solid state structures of these azaacenes, which are not only of interest for optoelectronics but also as building blocks for supramolecular chemistry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
macrocycles can be obtained from linear N-heteroace- nes by simple synthetic procedures and can be used as emitters in OLEDs.
the phenylene-bridges have little influence on the optical properties of the macrocycles.
the electronic properties of the cyclic azaacenes are largely independent of their molecular structure.
